# 1. SETUP & PACKAGES
```{r}
#We start off by installing all the packages needed to run the code in this script.Next to each package is a brief explanation of its function

library(tidyverse) #Data manipulation and ggplot
library(lubridate) #Data handling
library(TTR) #These are our technical indicators (RSI, MACD, SMA, etc.). Their purpose will be further explained later in ########[]########
library(caret) #Machine Learning framework (for training and comparing models)
library(corrplot) #Correlation plots in EDA
library(randomForest) #Random Forest model
library(gbm) #Gradient boosting model
library(pROC)# Roc curves and AUC scoring

# Neural network package: 
#Keras will be used to define neural networks in R.
#We also need a package that will run the neural network. 
install.packages("reticulate")
library(reticulate) #This package installs and manages the correct python version needed for the back-end.
reticulate::install_python(version = "3.10.12")
#The old "keras" package is deprecated. To work around this we simply install keras3
install.packages("keras3")
library(keras3) 


set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
```

# 2. LOAD DATA
```{r}
#The data used 
data_path <- "S&P500 price data.csv"

sp500_raw <- readr::read_csv(data_path)

# Basic checks
view (sp500_raw)
glimpse(sp500_raw)
summary(sp500_raw)

# Ensure Date column is Date class and data is sorted
sp500_raw <- sp500_raw %>%
mutate(Date = as.Date(Date))

sp500_raw <- sp500_raw %>% arrange(Date)

```

# 3. FEATURE ENGINEERING (TARGET + TECHNICAL INDICATORS)
```{r}
# 3.1 Create target: next-day direction (Up=1, Down=0)
sp500 <- sp500_raw %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  mutate(
    Close_lead = lead(Close), #this is tomorrow's close
    direction = if_else(Close_lead > Close, 1L, 0L)
  ) %>%
  drop_na(direction)

table(sp500$direction)
mean(sp500$direction)  # proportion of "Up" days


# 3.2 Create technical indicators (at least 10 features)
# Using the TTR package; we’ll create typical indicators:

sp500_fe <- sp500 %>%
  mutate(
    ret      = Close / lag(Close) - 1, # Daily return
    rsi_14   = RSI(Close, n = 14), # RSI(14)
    sma_10   = SMA(Close, n = 10), # SMA(10)
    sma_50   = SMA(Close, n = 50), # SMA(50)
    sma_200  = SMA(Close, n = 200), # SMA(200)
    macd_val = MACD(Close, nFast = 12, nSlow = 26, nSig = 9)[, "macd"],# MACD
    macd_sig = MACD(Close, nFast = 12, nSlow = 26, nSig = 9)[, "signal"],# Signal
    bbands   = BBands(Close, n = 20, sd = 2)[, "pctB"],# Bollinger %B
    vol_20   = runSD(ret, n = 20),# Rolling volatility
    mom_10   = momentum(Close, n = 10) # Momentum
  )

# Stochastic oscillator needs High, Low, Close
stoch_vals <- stoch(sp500_fe[, c("High", "Low", "Close")])
sp500_fe$stoch_k <- stoch_vals[, "fastK"]
sp500_fe$stoch_d <- stoch_vals[, "fastD"]

# Remove rows with NA created by rolling calculations
sp500_fe <- sp500_fe %>% drop_na()

# There is no volume data for the years before 1950. Therefore remove all rows before 1950 for better quality of models.

sp500_fe <- sp500_fe %>% 
  filter(Volume > 0)

# Keep final modelling data set: response + predictors
sp500_model <- sp500_fe %>%
  select(
    direction,
    ret, rsi_14, sma_10, sma_50, sma_200,
    macd_val, macd_sig, bbands, vol_20, mom_10,
    stoch_k, stoch_d, Volume
  )

glimpse(sp500_model)
summary(sp500_model)

```
# 4. TRAIN–TEST SPLIT (TIME-AWARE)
```{r}
# Number of observations
n <- nrow(sp500_model)

# Use 70% of the earliest data for training, 30% of the latest data for testing
train_prop <- 0.7
train_end  <- floor(train_prop * n)

train_idx <- 1:train_end
test_idx  <- (train_end + 1):n

train_data <- sp500_model[train_idx, ]
test_data  <- sp500_model[test_idx, ]

# Quick checks
nrow(train_data)
nrow(test_data)

# Class balance in each split
table(train_data$direction)
prop.table(table(train_data$direction))

table(test_data$direction)
prop.table(table(test_data$direction))

```

# 5. PREPROCESSING (SCALING, FACTORS, ETC.)
```{r}
# caret prefers factor response for classification
train_data$direction <- factor(train_data$direction, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Down", "Up"))
test_data$direction  <- factor(test_data$direction,  levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Down", "Up"))

# Create a recipe for scaling/centering predictors
library(recipes)

rec <- recipe(direction ~ ., data = train_data) %>%
  step_center(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_scale(all_predictors())

prep_rec  <- prep(rec)
# Apply recipe to training and test sets
train_x   <- bake(prep_rec, new_data = train_data)
test_x    <- bake(prep_rec, new_data = test_data)

# Check processed data
glimpse(train_x)

# Common trainControl for all models
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "cv",
  number = 5,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  savePredictions = "final"
)

```


# 6. MODELS

##6.1 Logistic Regression (GLM)
```{r}
set.seed(123)

mod_glm <- train(
  direction ~ .,           # use all other columns to predict direction
  data      = train_x,
  method    = "glm",
  family    = binomial,    # logistic regression
  trControl = ctrl,        # CV + class probs + ROC
  metric    = "ROC"        # optimise AUC
)

mod_glm              # CV results
summary(mod_glm$finalModel)   # GLM coefficients etc.

#Predictions on the test set

glm_probs <- predict(mod_glm, newdata = test_x, type = "prob")[, "Up"]  # P(Up)
glm_pred  <- predict(mod_glm, newdata = test_x)                         # class labels

# Confusion matrix
cm_glm <- confusionMatrix(glm_pred, test_x$direction, positive = "Up")
cm_glm

# ROC curve and AUC
roc_glm <- roc(
  response  = test_x$direction,
  predictor = glm_probs,
  levels    = c("Down", "Up"),
  direction = "<"
)

auc_glm <- auc(roc_glm)
auc_glm

plot(roc_glm, main = "GLM ROC Curve", print.auc = TRUE)
```
##6.2 Random Forest

```{r}
set.seed(123)

mod_rf <- train(
  direction ~ .,
  data      = train_x,
  method    = "rf",
  trControl = ctrl,      # CV + ROC
  tuneLength = 5,        # Try 5 different mtry values
  metric    = "ROC"      # Optimise AUC during CV
)

mod_rf                     # CV results
varImp(mod_rf) %>% plot(main = "Random Forest Variable Importance")

#Predictions on test data

rf_probs <- predict(mod_rf, newdata = test_x, type = "prob")[, "Up"]
rf_pred  <- predict(mod_rf, newdata = test_x)

# Confusion matrix
cm_rf <- confusionMatrix(rf_pred, test_x$direction, positive = "Up")
cm_rf

# ROC and AUC
roc_rf <- roc(
  response  = test_x$direction,
  predictor = rf_probs,
  levels    = c("Down", "Up"),
  direction = "<"
)

auc_rf <- auc(roc_rf)
auc_rf

plot(roc_rf, main = "Random Forest ROC Curve", print.auc = TRUE)

# Variable importance
rf_imp <- varImp(mod_rf)
print(rf_imp)
plot(rf_imp, main = "Random Forest Variable Importance")
```

## 6.3 Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM)
```{r}
set.seed(123)

mod_gbm <- train(
  direction ~ .,
  data       = train_x,
  method     = "gbm",
  trControl  = ctrl,        # CV + ROC
  verbose    = FALSE,
  tuneLength = 5,           # try 5 combinations of depth/trees/shrinkage
  metric     = "ROC"      # optimise AUC
)

mod_gbm     # CV results
varImp(mod_gbm) %>% plot(main = "GBM Variable Importance")

#Predictions on test data

gbm_probs <- predict(mod_gbm, newdata = test_x, type = "prob")[, "Up"]
gbm_pred  <- predict(mod_gbm, newdata = test_x)

# Confusion Matrix
cm_gbm <- confusionMatrix(gbm_pred, test_x$direction, positive = "Up")
cm_gbm

# ROC and AUC
roc_gbm <- roc(
  response  = test_x$direction,
  predictor = gbm_probs,
  levels    = c("Down", "Up"),
  direction = "<"
)

auc_gbm <- auc(roc_gbm)
auc_gbm

plot(roc_gbm, main = "GBM ROC Curve", print.auc = TRUE)
```

## 6.4 Neural Network (Keras)

```{r}
library(keras3)
# 1. Prepare matrices for keras3

x_train_mat <- train_x %>%
  dplyr::select(-direction) %>%
  as.matrix()

x_test_mat <- test_x %>%
  dplyr::select(-direction) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Convert factor response to numeric 0/1
y_train_vec <- ifelse(train_x$direction == "Up", 1, 0)
y_test_vec  <- ifelse(test_x$direction == "Up", 1, 0)

num_features <- ncol(x_train_mat)

# 2. Define the model architecture

dnn_model <- keras3::keras_model_sequential() |>
  keras3::layer_dense(units = 32, activation = "relu", input_shape = num_features) |>
  keras3::layer_dropout(rate = 0.3) |>
  keras3::layer_dense(units = 16, activation = "relu") |>
  keras3::layer_dropout(rate = 0.3) |>
  keras3::layer_dense(units = 1, activation = "sigmoid")

dnn_model |> summary()

# 3. Compile the model 

dnn_model |>
  compile(
    loss      = "binary_crossentropy",
    optimizer = optimizer_adam(),
    metrics   = "accuracy"
  )

# 4. Fit the model

history <- dnn_model |>
  fit(
    x = x_train_mat,
    y = y_train_vec,
    validation_split = 0.2,
    epochs = 50,
    batch_size = 32,
    verbose = 1
  )

plot(history)

# 5. Evaluate on test set

dnn_probs <- dnn_model |>
  predict(x_test_mat) |>
  as.vector()

# Turn probabilities into class labels using 0.5 threshold
dnn_pred <- ifelse(dnn_probs > 0.5, "Up", "Down") |>
  factor(levels = c("Down", "Up"))

# Confusion matrix
cm_dnn <- confusionMatrix(dnn_pred, test_x$direction, positive = "Up")
cm_dnn

# ROC and AUC
roc_dnn <- roc(
  response  = test_x$direction,
  predictor = dnn_probs,
  levels    = c("Down", "Up"),
  direction = "<"
)

auc_dnn <- auc(roc_dnn)
auc_dnn

plot(roc_dnn, main = "Neural Network ROC Curve", print.auc = TRUE)
```

# 7. COMPARISON SUMMARY
```{r}
results_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Model     = c("Logistic Regression (GLM)",
                "Random Forest",
                "Gradient Boosting (GBM)",
                "Neural Network (DNN)"),
  
  Accuracy  = c(
    cm_glm$overall["Accuracy"],
    cm_rf$overall["Accuracy"],
    cm_gbm$overall["Accuracy"],
    cm_dnn$overall["Accuracy"]
  ),

  Balanced_Accuracy = c(
    cm_glm$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"],
    cm_rf$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"],
    cm_gbm$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"],
    cm_dnn$byClass["Balanced Accuracy"]
  ),

  AUC = c(
    auc_glm,
    auc_rf,
    auc_gbm,
    auc_dnn
  )
)

# Display the table
results_tbl

knitr::kable(
  results_tbl,
  digits = 4,
  caption = "Model Performance Comparison (Test Set)"
)

print(results_tbl)

# Neat graphic: compare models visually

library(tidyverse)

# 1. Convert to long format for ggplot
results_long <- results_tbl |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Accuracy, Balanced_Accuracy, AUC),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

# 2. Make a grouped bar chart
ggplot(results_long, aes(x = Model, y = Value, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.48, 0.56)) +  # zoom into the interesting range
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Model Performance Comparison (Test Set)",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Score",
    fill = "Metric"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
  )
```
